sentences.en: How do you think they solved this problem?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他们是如何解决这个问题的？

sentences.en: That would be a way to get them to think about the aspect of the content that I think was meant to be the focus.
sentences.zh: 这将是一种引导他们思考本应成为核心内容的某个方面的方法。

sentences.en: You talk about another technique called elaborative interrogation.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了另一种叫做“精细化审问”的技术。

sentences.en: What is this, Dan, and how does it work?
sentences.zh: 丹，这是什么？它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: This is a technique to improve comprehension and also improve memory,
sentences.zh: 这是一项旨在提高理解力和记忆力的技术，

sentences.en: where as you're reading something, you pose questions to yourself and try to answer the questions.
sentences.zh: 即当你在阅读某样东西时，向自己提出问题并试图回答这些问题。

sentences.en: It's even more effective if before you start reading the text,
sentences.zh: 如果在开始阅读文本之前，

sentences.en: you actually look ahead a little bit and make some predictions about what you think you're likely to learn when you read this text and then pose questions based on that little preview that you do.
sentences.zh: 你能稍微提前看一下，并对阅读该文本时可能会学到的内容做出一些预测，然后根据这个简短的预览提出问题，那就更有效了。

sentences.en: And then when you're reading the text, you're thinking about, did I pose good questions?
sentences.zh: 然后，当你在阅读文本时，你会思考：我提出的问题好吗？

sentences.en: Is this actually what the text is about?
sentences.zh: 这真的是文本所讲的内容吗？

sentences.en: And if it is, what are the answers to those questions?
sentences.zh: 如果是的话，这些问题的答案是什么？

sentences.en: And if it's not, what are some better questions?
sentences.zh: 如果不是的话，有哪些更好的问题？

sentences.en: I mean, and all of this in some ways goes back to that idea we talked about, which is that we remember what it is we're mentally engaged with.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某种程度上，这一切都可以追溯到我们讨论过的一个观点，那就是我们会记住那些我们在精神上投入其中的东西。

sentences.en: And so if you want to remember things, you have to find ways to actually engage with the material, not just simply be a passive recipient for it,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想记住事情，你必须找到真正与材料互动的方法，而不仅仅是被动地接受它，

sentences.en: but actually think about it, engage it, probe it, try and see the connections between that and other ideas, contest it, argue with it.
sentences.zh: 而是真正去思考它、参与其中、探究它、试图找出它与其他观点之间的联系、质疑它、与它争论。

sentences.en: That's the way you actually remember the material, not just simply listening to it.
sentences.zh: 这才是真正记住材料的方法，而不仅仅是听它讲。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And these little tricks, I think, help because, again, one of the things that it's hard to do is sort of tell yourself,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这些小技巧很有帮助，因为正如我所说，很难做到的一点是告诫自己，

sentences.en: OK, now I'm really going to think deeply about this.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在我要真正深入地思考这个问题了。

sentences.en: You need something more concrete.
sentences.zh: 你需要更具体的东西。

sentences.en: So the technique like, well, you know, look at the subheadings and try and generate some questions based on that.
sentences.zh: 所以像这样的技术，比如，看一看小标题，并试着据此生成一些问题。

sentences.en: That gives the mind something to work with where you see what the path forward is instead of just telling people, well, really think about what it means.
sentences.zh: 这能给大脑提供一些可以思考的东西，让你看到前进的道路，而不是仅仅告诉人们“好好想想它的意思”。

sentences.en: Another way of harnessing meaning is to frame the information that you're processing in the form of a story.
sentences.zh: 利用意义的另一种方法是将你正在处理的信息构建为故事的形式。

sentences.en: Tell me about this idea, Dan.
sentences.zh: 丹，跟我讲讲这个想法。

sentences.en: Yes, stories are very effective because stories have connections.
sentences.zh: 是的，故事非常有效，因为故事具有联系。

sentences.en: Stories have causality in them, right?
sentences.zh: 故事中包含因果关系，对吧？

sentences.en: It's in the nature of stories that event B was caused by event A.
sentences.zh: 事件B是由事件A引起的，这是故事的本质。

sentences.en: And so you can think about when there's content that you would like to master,
sentences.zh: 因此你可以考虑，当有你想要掌握的内容时，

sentences.en: thinking of whether or not it fits well into a story context can be a really effective way of organizing it.
sentences.zh: 思考它是否能很好地契合故事的语境，可以成为组织这些内容的一种非常有效的方法。

sentences.en: And I understand there's been research that is tested when people get information just as information.
sentences.zh: 据我所了解，曾有研究测试过当人们单纯作为信息接收信息时，

sentences.en: And when people get information in the form of a story, there are differences in how well people remember the information?
sentences.zh: 以及当人们以故事形式接收信息时，人们对信息的记忆效果是否存在差异？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: It's very clever experiments where they took basically the same set of facts that they were hoping to impart to the people who are going to be reading it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常巧妙的实验，他们基本上采用了希望传达给阅读者的同一组事实。

sentences.en: And some people read what you would just think of as a straightforward expository essay that laid out the facts.
sentences.zh: 一部分人阅读的是你所认为的直白陈述事实的说明文。

sentences.en: And then other people had the same facts sort of shaped into a story format.
sentences.zh: 而另一部分人阅读的则是将相同的事实塑造为故事形式的内容。

sentences.en: Again, the emphasis within the story was on causality connections among these various pieces.
sentences.zh: 同样，故事中的重点在于这些不同部分之间的因果联系。

sentences.en: And what they found was that people who read it in a story format remembered the information better.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，以故事形式阅读的人对信息的记忆效果更好。

sentences.en: And in some ways, I think this speaks to the idea that what you're talking about is really not just discrete pieces of information,
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，我认为这说明了你所谈论的其实不仅是零散的信息片段，

sentences.en: but the architecture of how all this information fits together.
sentences.zh: 而是所有这些信息如何组合在一起的架构。

sentences.en: And of course, in a well-constructed story, you don't just have a whole bunch of discrete pieces of information.
sentences.zh: 当然，在一个构建良好的故事中，并不只有一堆零散的信息片段。

sentences.en: You actually have the entire architecture of the Lego building, if you will, with all the pieces sort of connected to one another.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，你实际上拥有了整个乐高建筑的架构，所有的部件都以某种方式相互连接。

sentences.en: So when you're asked to identify any individual piece, you have a sense of where it sits in the overall scheme.
sentences.zh: 因此，当被要求识别任何单独的部件时，你对它在整体方案中的位置会有所感知。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: I mean, the connections are so important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些联系太重要了。

sentences.en: And I mean, some everyday evidence about this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这有一些日常的证据。

sentences.en: Think about the last time someone, you went to a movie and the next day someone asked you, oh, you saw that movie.
sentences.zh: 想想看，上一次有人……你去看了一部电影，第二天有人问你，哦，你看过那部电影了。

sentences.en: What was that about?
sentences.zh: 那是讲什么的？

sentences.en: No one ever says, oh, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人会说，哦，我不知道。

sentences.en: Like, I didn't study it.
sentences.zh: 就像，我没有研究过它。

sentences.en: You know, I just saw it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我只是看了看。

sentences.en: I can't remember it.
sentences.zh: 我记不清了。

sentences.en: No, the memory just comes for free when you're engaged with a story.
sentences.zh: 不，当你投入到一个故事中时，记忆就会自然而然地涌现。

sentences.en: And it is, as you say, it's all these Lego pieces fitting together because that's so intrinsic to the way memory works.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所说，这就是所有乐高积木拼合在一起的过程，因为这正是记忆工作方式的内在本质。

sentences.en: You remember things based on cues.
sentences.zh: 你是根据线索来记忆事物的。

sentences.en: You get a hint.
sentences.zh: 你会得到一个提示。

sentences.en: I say this and then, you know, I say salt.
sentences.zh: 我说出这个，然后，你知道，我说出盐。

sentences.en: That makes you think of pepper.
sentences.zh: 这会让你想到胡椒。

sentences.en: These two things are connected in memory.
sentences.zh: 这两样东西在记忆中是连在一起的。

sentences.en: So in a story, everything is connected to something else.
sentences.zh: 所以在故事中，每样东西都与其他东西相连。

sentences.en: So it's sort of like at the beginning of the story,
sentences.zh: 所以这就有点像在故事的开头，

sentences.en: it's like you're pulling out this very fine chain and the little pieces of the story are like little charms attached to the chain.
sentences.zh: 就像你拉出一条非常精致的链子，故事中的小片段就像挂在链子上的小饰品。

sentences.en: You just keep tugging and it keeps coming out and it's easy to remember.
sentences.zh: 你只要一直拉，它就会不断出来，而且很容易记住。

sentences.en: You and others have talked about different elements in stories that are worth thinking about.
sentences.zh: 你和其他人都讨论过故事中值得思考的不同元素。

sentences.en: If we wanted to construct stories to remember things, what are these elements that we should focus on then?
sentences.zh: 如果我们想构建故事来记住事情，那么我们应该关注哪些元素呢？

sentences.en: Conflict is the way it's usually described in story structure.
sentences.zh: 在故事结构中，通常将其描述为冲突。

sentences.en: So in Star Wars, you know, is Luke going to be able to save the civilization by destroying the Death Star?
sentences.zh: 所以在《星球大战》中，你知道，卢克能通过摧毁死星来拯救文明吗？

sentences.en: He needs something to fight againSt.
sentences.zh: 他需要一个与之对抗的对象。

sentences.en: So it's going to be Darth Vader.
sentences.zh: 所以那个人将是达斯·维达。

sentences.en: With our combined strength, we can end this destructive conflict and bring order to the galaxy.
sentences.zh: 凭借我们共同的力量，我们可以结束这场破坏性的冲突，为银河系带来秩序。

sentences.en: I'll never join you!
sentences.zh: 我永远不会加入你！

sentences.en: And then there, again, when you're thinking about story structure, you're usually thinking about multiple pieces.
sentences.zh: 然后，再次强调，当你考虑故事结构时，你通常会考虑多个部分。

sentences.en: So the other aspect, in addition to conflict, is complication.
sentences.zh: 因此，除了冲突之外，另一个方面是复杂情况。

sentences.en: So the first try at the solution to the problem that you've figured out usually doesn't work for one reason or another.
sentences.zh: 所以，你针对想出的问题所做出的第一种解决方案通常由于某种原因而行不通。

sentences.en: That's a complication.
sentences.zh: 这就是复杂情况。

sentences.en: Then there's a sub-problem that you have to figure out.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一个你需要解决的子问题。

sentences.en: And again, that makes for very nice connections that helps you sort of keep it all organized in your mind and easier to remember.
sentences.zh: 同样，这创造了非常好的联系，帮助你在脑海中保持所有内容的条理，并且更容易记住。

sentences.en: Can you also talk about the role that characters play in our memories?
sentences.zh: 你还能谈谈角色在我们的记忆中扮演的角色吗？

sentences.en: The characters that we encounter in stories would seem to be an important component of what makes stories memorable.
sentences.zh: 我们在故事中遇到的角色似乎是使故事令人难忘的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And again, you know, if there are people in what you're trying to remember, that's going to be really helpful.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你试图记住的东西里面有人，那将会非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Individual personalities help.
sentences.zh: 独特的个性会有所帮助。

sentences.en: Distinctiveness helps memory.
sentences.zh: 独特性有助于记忆。

sentences.en: Things that stand out because they're unlike other things that you've encountered.
sentences.zh: 那些因为与你遇到的其他事物不同而脱颖而出的事物。

sentences.en: That's a very general principle of memory, that things that are really distinctive are much easier to remember.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常普遍的记忆原则，即真正具有独特性的事物更容易被记住。

sentences.en: So if you've got individual people, then that's great.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有具体的人物，那就太棒了。

sentences.en: If you don't have individual people, you can still think of something analogous in your story where sort of the action is.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有具体的人物，你仍然可以在你的故事中想出类似的东西，也就是情节发生的地方。

sentences.en: I was describing this to a physicist, and he immediately said energy.
sentences.zh: 我曾向一位物理学家描述过这一点，他立刻说出了能量。

sentences.en: In any physical system, I always look for the energy because that's where the action is going to be.
sentences.zh: 在任何物理系统中，我总是寻找能量，因为那是行动将要发生的地方。

sentences.en: And I don't know enough physics to really evaluate whether or not that was right, but his eyes lit up when he was telling me that.
sentences.zh: 我对物理学的了解还不足以真正评估这是否正确，但当他告诉我这些时，他的眼睛亮了起来。

sentences.en: So that's a way of thinking about the role of character, not just in stories where they're actually people, but in other types of stories as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种思考角色作用的方式，不仅在那些真正有人物的故事中，在其他类型的的故事中也是如此。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking about plays or movies, you know, a movie like Beautiful Mind, I think, did far more to popularize the ideas of John Nash, the mathematician,
sentences.zh: 我在想戏剧或电影，你知道，像《美丽心灵》这样的电影，我认为它在普及数学家约翰·纳什的观点方面，

sentences.en: than any number of mathematics textbooks.
sentences.zh: 起到的作用远超无数本数学教科书。

sentences.en: And Hamilton, the play, probably did more for, you know, U.S.
sentences.zh: 而戏剧《汉密尔顿》，对于你知道的美国

sentences.en: history and American history and people, students understanding American history than, you know, countless history classes.
sentences.zh: 历史、美国历史以及人们、学生对美国历史的理解，其作用可能超过了无数的历史课。

sentences.en: After the war, I went back to New York.
sentences.zh: 战后，我回到了纽约。

sentences.en: Yes, those were beautiful examples of character-driven stories.
sentences.zh: 是的，这些都是以人物为驱动的故事的美丽例证。

sentences.en: Even though we started at the very same time, Alexander Hamilton began to climb.
sentences.zh: 尽管我们起步于完全相同的时刻，亚历山大·汉密尔顿开始向上攀登。

sentences.en: How to account for his rise to the top?
sentences.zh: 如何解释他能登上顶峰？

sentences.en: Man, the man is non-stop.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这个人简直势不可挡。

sentences.en: Gentlemen of the jury, I'm curious.
sentences.zh: 陪审团的先生们，我很好奇。

sentences.en: So sometimes, Dan, the information we have to memorize is not in itself very meaningful.
sentences.zh: 所以有时候，丹，我们必须记住的信息本身并不是很有意义。

sentences.en: So let's say you're trying to remember the names of all the presidents of the United States.
sentences.zh: 假设你试图记住美国所有总统的名字。

sentences.en: There's obviously no meaning to the names.
sentences.zh: 这些名字显然没有任何意义。

sentences.en: There's no story to connect all the names together.
sentences.zh: 没有任何故事可以将所有这些名字串联在一起。

sentences.en: What do we do?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: The go-to method here is a mnemonic, and the mnemonics are ways of lending meaning to something that doesn't have any meaning,
sentences.zh: 这里首选的方法是助记符，助记符是将意义赋予原本没有任何意义的事物的方法，

sentences.en: or other times it's another sort of a trick that helps the information become easier to pull out of memory.
sentences.zh: 或者在其他时候，它是另一种有助于使信息更容易从记忆中提取出来的技巧。

sentences.en: Have you done this?
sentences.zh: 你做过这个吗？

sentences.en: Are there mnemonics that you still remember from your childhood?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么助记符是你从童年一直记到现在的？

sentences.en: Absolutely, and in junior year of high school, my teacher asked all of us to memorize the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当然有，在高中的倒数第二年，我的老师要求我们所有人生动地按顺序记住美国

sentences.en: presidents in order and taught us a little mnemonic song to commit them to memory.
sentences.zh: 总统，并教了我们一首小助记歌把它印在脑海里。

sentences.en: I'm going to put you on the spot here, Dan.
sentences.zh: 丹，我要在这里当众考考你了。

sentences.en: Let's give it a go.
sentences.zh: 我们来试试吧。

sentences.en: And what does that stand for?
sentences.zh: 那代表什么意思？

sentences.en: I'm sort of starting to pick up the outlines of the names there.
sentences.zh: 我有点开始听出那些名字的轮廓了。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's the first letter of each president's name.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以它是每个总统名字的首字母。

sentences.en: So it starts, Wa, Jamah.
sentences.zh: 所以它是这样开始的：Wa, Jamah。

sentences.en: So Wa is Washington, Adams, Jamah, Jefferson, Madison, Monroe, Adams, J.V., Jackson, Van Buren.
sentences.zh: 所以Wa是华盛顿、亚当斯，Jamah是杰斐逊、麦迪逊、门罗、亚当斯，J.V.是杰克逊、范布伦。

sentences.en: And then occasionally you have to remember some things.
sentences.zh: 然后偶尔你必须记住一些东西。

sentences.en: So like Trumican is Truman, and then Ike for Eisenhower, and then it ends Ken for Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 比如Trumican是杜鲁门，然后Ike是艾森豪威尔，然后以肯尼迪的Ken结束。

sentences.en: So there are little bits in there where you have to do some interpretation, but of course that's not hard.
sentences.zh: 所以里面有一些你需要进行解释的小片段，但当然这并不难。

sentences.en: And I will say I probably recite that little rhyme to myself once or twice a year when for some reason I'm trying to think now who is probably president at that point.
sentences.zh: 而且我要说的是，我大概一年会对自己背诵一两次那个小顺口溜，当时出于某种原因我正试图想现在那个时候谁可能是总统。

sentences.en: Needless to say, you have to be kind of quiet when you do it.
sentences.zh: 不用说，当你这样做的时候，你必须保持安静。

sentences.en: Socially, it's a little awkward.
sentences.zh: 在社交场合，这有点尴尬。

sentences.en: So we've talked about how easy it is for us to feel a sense of familiarity with a given set of facts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们讨论了我们对一组特定的事实产生熟悉感是多么容易。

sentences.en: But instead of familiarity, you suggest that we need to adopt a new standard of what it means to know something,
sentences.zh: 但你建议我们不要追求熟悉感，而是需要采纳关于了解某事的新标准，

sentences.en: something that can overcome our illusion of explanatory depth where we believe we know things better than we actually know them.
sentences.zh: 这种标准可以克服我们的解释深度错觉，即我们认为自己比实际更好地了解事物。

sentences.en: What is the technique that you suggest, Dan?
sentences.zh: 丹，你建议的技术是什么？

sentences.en: Most of the time, the technique is going to be posing the question to yourself and seeing whether or not you can explain it.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，这项技术就是向自己提出问题，看看你是否能够解释它。

sentences.en: I would elaborate on this a little bit.
sentences.zh: 对此我想稍微详细阐述一下。

sentences.en: I would say that the technique you use to test your memory should be a good fit for what you actually want to be able to do with the information.
sentences.zh: 我会说，你用来测试记忆力的技术应该非常适合你实际上希望能够用这些信息做的事情。

sentences.en: So, for example, this comes up a lot in the context of mathematics.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，这在数学语境中经常出现。

sentences.en: Students will learn a particular formula to solve a particular type of problem,
sentences.zh: 学生们将学习一个特定的公式来解决特定类型的问题，

sentences.en: and they learn it in the context of a word problem that's to do with football players, for example.
sentences.zh: 并且他们是在与橄榄球运动员有关的应用题语境中学习它的，例如。

sentences.en: And then on the test, the same principle is tested.
sentences.zh: 然后在考试中，测试的就是同一个原理。

sentences.en: They need to use the same formula, but now it's not football players.
sentences.zh: 他们需要使用相同的公式，但这次的主角不是足球运动员。

sentences.en: Now it's automobiles or something else.
sentences.zh: 现在换成了汽车或其他东西。

sentences.en: And they fail to recognize the information.
sentences.zh: 而他们却没能识别出其中的规律。

sentences.en: This is a different type of recognition, and it's actually much more difficult.
sentences.zh: 这是一种不同类型的识别，实际上要困难得多。

sentences.en: So, memory tends to cling to the examples that we initially encountered.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们的记忆往往会紧抓着最初遇到的例子不放。

sentences.en: So, you need to think about what am I actually wanting to do with this information?
sentences.zh: 因此，你需要思考：我实际上想用这些信息来做什么？

sentences.en: Do I need to be able to just describe it to others?
sentences.zh: 我只需要能够把它描述给别人听吗？

sentences.en: That's what we talked about as being more difficult than just recognizing it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们之前讨论过的，比单纯识别要更困难的那种情况。

sentences.en: Or do I need to be able to recognize it in new guises?
sentences.zh: 还是说我需要在新的伪装下认出它？

sentences.en: That's still more difficult.
sentences.zh: 那就更难了。

sentences.en: So, take the problem that was about football and take the problem that was about automobiles.
sentences.zh: 所以，拿那个关于足球的问题和那个关于汽车的问题来对比。

sentences.en: Take those two problems that look different on the surface and then describe how are these actually similar.
sentences.zh: 找出这两个表面上看起来不同的问题，然后描述它们实际上有哪些相似之处。

sentences.en: And Shankar, this actually follows the principle that you and I have been talking about before,
sentences.zh: 香卡，这其实符合你我之前一直在讨论的一个原则，

sentences.en: which is that memory sort of follows thought.
sentences.zh: 那就是记忆在某种程度上跟随思维。

sentences.en: What you're getting yourself to do by comparing those problems is thinking about what they have in common.
sentences.zh: 通过对比这些问题，你促使自己去思考它们的共同点。

sentences.en: You're thinking about that deep structure that they share.
sentences.zh: 你在思考它们所共享的深层结构。

sentences.en: And so, that's going to make you better appreciate that deep structure and be able to remember it and recognize it later in new probleMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，这会让你更好地理解这种深层结构，并在以后面对新问题时能够记住并认出它。

sentences.en: You know, so much of what we've been talking about, I think, goes back to that idea of almost probing our minds to find the weaknesses,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们谈论的很多内容，我觉得都归结于这样一个想法：几乎就像是在探测我们的大脑以寻找弱点，

sentences.en: to find the broken links in the chain.
sentences.zh: 去寻找链条中的断裂环节。

sentences.en: And that is just so hard to do, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 而这做起来真的太难了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because it's sort of constantly exposing us to the limits of our own knowledge, the limits of our own understanding.
sentences.zh: 因为它不断地让我们直面自己知识的极限、理解的极限。

sentences.en: It's forcing us to do the difficult thing of doing, you know, the push-ups where you're trying to clap as you're doing the push-ups.
sentences.zh: 它强迫我们去做那些高难度的事情，就像你做俯卧撑时还试图在空中击掌一样。

sentences.en: I think I'm trying to intuit why it is so many of us not only have bad memories, but why it's so difficult to fix those bad memories.
sentences.zh: 我想我是在试图直观地理解，为什么我们当中有那么多人不仅记性不好，而且为什么修复这些不好的记忆会如此困难。

sentences.en: It's just effortful.
sentences.zh: 这太费劲了。

sentences.en: And I think it's hard to face up to it.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得很难去正视它。

sentences.en: It's not fun to say like, oh, there's a whole lot here that I don't know.
sentences.zh: 承认“哦，这里有好多东西我都不知道”，这可一点也不好玩。

sentences.en: There's a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 有太多太多了。

sentences.en: Let me make a point of probing what I don't know.
sentences.zh: 让我特意去探测一下我所不知道的东西吧。

sentences.en: Let me find my weaknesses.
sentences.zh: 让我找出自己的弱点。

sentences.en: That takes, you know, ego strength to sort of be brave in that way and look at what we don't know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这需要自我力量，才能以那种方式保持勇敢，去审视我们未知的事物。

sentences.en: So even when we use very rigorous memory strategies, our memories may still fail us.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使我们使用了非常严谨的记忆策略，我们的记忆有时还是会让我们失望。

sentences.en: And you have learned to use external aids to help your memory.
sentences.zh: 而你已经学会使用外部辅助工具来帮助你的记忆。

sentences.en: I understand that, in fact, you might be a little obsessed with calendars and alarMs.
sentences.zh: 我听说，事实上，你可能有点沉迷于日历和闹钟。

sentences.en: Can you tell me about your various practices involving calendars and alarms, Dan?
sentences.zh: 丹，你能跟我聊聊你使用日历和闹钟的各种习惯吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm obsessed is probably fair.
sentences.zh: 对，说我沉迷大概并不过分。

sentences.en: My perspective memory is not very good.
sentences.zh: 我的前瞻性记忆不太好。

sentences.en: I don't remember to do things.
sentences.zh: 我经常记不住要去做事。

sentences.en: And so the way I deal with that is I've made a real habit of relying on my calendar.
sentences.zh: 所以我应对的方法是，养成了依赖日历的切实习惯。

sentences.en: And if it's not on my calendar, the odds that I'm going to remember it are very, very close to zero.
sentences.zh: 如果它没有记在我的日历上，我能记住它的概率就无限接近于零。

sentences.en: And I also make heavy use of alarms that are programmed in my phone.
sentences.zh: 而且我也大量使用手机里设置的闹钟。

sentences.en: And in a typical day, I'll have eight alarms or something like that going.
sentences.zh: 在平常的一天里，我大概会有八个闹钟在响个不停。

sentences.en: So you have something going off at 1125 to tell you something's happening at 1130.
sentences.zh: 所以你会在11点25分设置一个闹钟，提醒你11点30分有事要发生。

sentences.en: Pay attention.
sentences.zh: 注意啦。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, again, this is sort of facing up to weakness.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这同样也是在正视弱点。

sentences.en: I just live too much in my head.
sentences.zh: 我太活在自己的世界里了。

sentences.en: And I'm not aware enough of the world around me.
sentences.zh: 我对周围世界的感知不够敏锐。

sentences.en: And so I need something to sort of snap me out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以我需要某种东西来把我从这种状态中猛然唤醒。

sentences.en: I understand that this habit of relying on external memory saved the day for you at one point a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 我听说几年前，你这种依赖外部记忆的习惯曾在关键时刻救了你一命。

sentences.en: Tell me that story, Dan.
sentences.zh: 给我讲讲那个故事吧，丹。

sentences.en: This is five years ago, maybe.
sentences.zh: 大概是五年前吧。

sentences.en: And my wife had our three children out.
sentences.zh: 当时我妻子带着我们的三个孩子出去了。

sentences.en: They were all at an event that I was not at.
sentences.zh: 他们去参加一个我没有出席的活动。

sentences.en: And this was on a Sunday.
sentences.zh: 那是在一个星期天。

sentences.en: So this is pretty unusual for me with three small children.
sentences.zh: 所以对于要照顾三个小孩子的我来说，这相当罕见。

sentences.en: And so I was really enjoying myself.
sentences.zh: 因此我当时过得非常开心。

sentences.en: I'm sort of puttering around the house and doing little chores as we do on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 我大概是在家里转悠着，做点周日常做的小杂务。

sentences.en: And then I start to say I'm going to do a little work puttering.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始说我要一边转悠一边干点工作。

sentences.en: So I start answering email and so on.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始回复电子邮件等等。

sentences.en: And then at some point, I get an email where I need to put something in my calendar.
sentences.zh: 就在某个时刻，我收到了一封邮件，里面有些内容需要我记到日历上。

sentences.en: So I open my calendar, and I still remember the feeling of opening my calendar and perceiving on that day a red blob.
sentences.zh: 于是我打开日历，我至今还记得当时打开日历并看到那天有一个红色方块时的感觉。

sentences.en: Red means important.
sentences.zh: 红色意味着重要。

sentences.en: And it was one of those things where, like, time slows down.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像是时间变慢了。

sentences.en: And I'm like, that can't be right.
sentences.zh: 我在想：这不可能吧。

sentences.en: And I go and look at what it is, and I realize I have an airplane I'm supposed to be on in 75 minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后我去查看那是什么事，赫然发现我必须在75分钟后赶上一架飞机。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And the airplane, I was supposed to go to a city in the Midwest, and I was supposed to give a talk the next day.
sentences.zh: 而且那趟航班我是要去中西部的一个城市，第二天我还得做一场演讲。

sentences.en: I wasn't packed.
sentences.zh: 我根本还没收拾行李。

sentences.en: I had absolutely no idea what the talk was supposed to be that I was supposed to give.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道自己到时候要做一场什么样的演讲。

sentences.en: The airport's about a half an hour away.
sentences.zh: 去机场大约要半个小时车程。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So sort of for my life, I threw things in a suitcase, and it all ended up fine.
sentences.zh: 为了保命似的，我把东西一股脑塞进手提箱，最后总算一切顺利。

sentences.en: But that was a very close call.
sentences.zh: 但那可真是险象环生。

sentences.zh: 今天节目的最后，我们为您带来姊妹节目《我无名英雄》中的一个故事。

sentences.en: This My Unsung Hero segment is brought to you by T-Mobile for Business.
sentences.zh: 本期《我无名英雄》由 T-Mobile 企业版倾情赞助。

sentences.en: Our story comes from Sabrina Kronk.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事来自萨布丽娜·克朗克。

sentences.en: 20 years ago, Sabrina was a newly single mother living near Nashville.
sentences.zh: 20年前，萨布丽娜是一位住在纳什维尔附近的新单亲妈妈。

sentences.en: Things were tough financially, but she just landed a new job, and life was looking up.
sentences.zh: 当时经济状况很拮据，但她刚刚找到了一份新工作，生活正迎来转机。

sentences.en: That is, until one fall morning, when she got into her car to take her daughter to daycare, and the car wouldn't start.
sentences.zh: 直到某个秋天的早晨，她上车准备送女儿去日托中心时，车却怎么也打不着火了。

sentences.en: I had a Jeep Grand Cherokee that had over 250,000 miles, and I walked out to my car, put my three and a half year old daughter in her car seat, jumped in the front seat,
sentences.zh: 我有一辆切诺基吉普，里程已经超过了25万英里。我走到车前，把三岁半的女儿抱进安全座椅，坐进前排，

sentences.en: and put the keys in the ignition.
sentences.zh: 把钥匙插进点火开关。

sentences.en: I tried to turn the ignition, tried to turn the keys, and immediately heard this clicking noise, and, you know, my heart just sunk.
sentences.zh: 我尝试转动点火开关、转动钥匙，然后立刻听到了一声咔哒声，你知道，我的心一下子就沉了下去。

sentences.en: I thought, what is wrong now?
sentences.zh: 我在想：这次又是哪里坏了？

sentences.en: I had had my car in the shop multiple times over the past couple of weeks and months.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几个星期和几个月里，我的车已经进过好几次修理厂了。

sentences.en: Finances were just so limited at that point, and I'd already been pouring a lot of money into the car.
sentences.zh: 当时手头实在太紧，我已经往这辆车里砸了不少钱了。

sentences.en: The car eventually rumbled to a start, and I knew I had to drive straight to the service center at the car dealership and not stop anywhere else so I could get there in one piece,
sentences.zh: 车子最终轰鸣着启动了，我知道我必须直接开到汽车经销商的服务中心，中途绝对不能停在任何地方，这样才能完好无缺地赶到那里，

sentences.en: and hopefully it wouldn't break down on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 祈祷它不会在路边抛锚。

sentences.en: So we drove straight to the dealership, pulled into the service bay,
sentences.zh: 于是我们直接开车去了经销商那里，驶入服务车间，

sentences.en: and the service technicians started taking out my daughter's car seat and putting it in the courtesy car that would drive us to her daycare and work.
sentences.zh: 服务技师们开始把我女儿的安全座椅拆下来，装进将送我们去日托中心和工作单位的代步车里。

sentences.en: And I realized they had done it so many times that it was like we had our own personal pit crew.
sentences.zh: 我意识到他们之前已经做过无数次这样的事了，感觉我们就像拥有了自己的专属维修团队。

sentences.en: You know, you pull in, and they start taking care of things without even being told what to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你把车开进来，甚至不用吩咐他们做什么，他们就已经开始料理一切了。

sentences.en: They just knew to transfer everything.
sentences.zh: 他们自然而然就知道要把所有东西都搬过去。

sentences.en: They would even shuttle us to the front of the line, like they didn't want her to have to wait or me to have to wait.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至会把我们带到队伍最前面，好像他们不想让她或者我多等哪怕一会儿。

sentences.en: They drove me to her daycare, and then I walked to work, which wasn't far.
sentences.zh: 他们开车送我去了女儿的日托中心，然后我步行去上班，路程并不远。

sentences.en: And so at the end of the day, they called me, told me the courtesy car was on the way, and that it would be ready when I got there that afternoon to pick up.
sentences.zh: 到了傍晚，他们打电话给我，说代步车正在路上，等我那天下午去取车时一切都已经准备好了。

sentences.en: So I'll walk up to the cashier after we arrived, and she told me there was no charge.
sentences.zh: 等我们到达后，我走到收银台前，她告诉我这次不收任何费用。

sentences.en: They had miraculously found the part I needed at no cost, and I said, could you check that?
sentences.zh: 他们奇迹般地免费找到了我需要的零件。我说：你能帮我核实一下吗？

sentences.en: Like, what is the labor cost going to be today?
sentences.zh: 今天的工时费大概是多少？

sentences.en: And she said that the service technicians had donated their labor, and I just couldn't believe what I was hearing.
sentences.zh: 她说服务技师们捐出了他们的工时费，我简直不敢相信自己的耳朵。

sentences.en: So I asked her if she would please check with the manager.
sentences.zh: 于是我请她跟经理再确认一下。

sentences.en: I just wanted to make sure, and he came over to me and just told me just to not worry about it.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保万无一失，然后他朝我走过来，告诉我不用担心这一切，

sentences.en: Everything was taken care of, just to focus on taking care of my daughter.
sentences.zh: 所有费用都搞定了，让我只管专心照顾女儿就行。

sentences.en: I could barely speak.
sentences.zh: 我激动得几乎说不出话来。

sentences.en: Tears filled my eyes, and he ushered me quickly in my car and then kind of gave me two taps on the top of the car, like, let's go.
sentences.zh: 泪水盈满眼眶，他快步把我送上车，然后在我车顶上轻轻拍了两下，仿佛在说：走吧。

sentences.en: I'll just never forget that kindness and generosity.
sentences.zh: 那份善良与慷慨我永远不会忘记。

sentences.en: I mean, in them doing that, it made it possible for us to survive financially the rest of the month.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他们那样做，让我们得以在经济上挺过那个月的余下日子。

sentences.en: Whenever I think about that time in my life, I think about not only that crew, but all the other people that helped us.
sentences.zh: 每当我回想起我人生中的那段时光，我不仅会想起那个团队，还会想起所有其他帮助过我们的人。

sentences.en: Just having that kind of kindness in a moment where you're like, what now?
sentences.zh: 当你处在那种“接下来该怎么办？”，

sentences.en: What else do I have to deal with?
sentences.zh: “我还要应付什么麻烦？”的绝境时，能感受到那样的善意……

sentences.en: They say when you're at the end of your lifeline, you know, tie a piece of string on it and hang on.
sentences.zh: 人们常说，当你走到生命尽头时，系上一根绳子坚持住。

sentences.en: Well, they allowed me to do that that day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那天他们让我做到了这一点。

sentences.en: Sabrina Kronk of Nashville, Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 田纳西州纳什维尔的萨布丽娜·克朗克。

sentences.en: Her daughter Katie is now an adult.
sentences.zh: 她的女儿凯蒂现在已经长大成人了。

sentences.zh: 下周，我们将聚焦愤世嫉俗心态，为今年的 U2.0 系列节目画上句号。

sentences.en: So it's almost as though if social connection is medicine, it doesn't work for cynics.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，如果说社交联系是一剂良药，那它对愤世嫉俗的人却不起作用。

sentences.en: It's almost as though they have, you know, they're resistant to this medication that helps the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 这就好像他们对这种能帮助我们其他人的药物产生了某种抗药性。

sentences.zh: 愤世嫉俗如何伤害了我们，以及我们该如何抵制它的影响。
